notes: Artifacts: ten one-of-a-kind relics of war, sold only by merchants. The Ninth Bell tolls and stuns everything near it, the Comet Lance calls down comets, the Sunforged Aegis raises domes of sunlight, the Drowned Mirror brings a double into battle, the Tempest Standard calls lightning, and more
You can now hold up to 2500 gold (3500 with the Tithe Box)
The maximum level is now 10: one more unit on the field, and the best odds of rare recruits. Late enemy armies grow to match
Every unit has a line of its own story on its card
Clearer text throughout: an up-to-date Guide and Boot Camp tips, and unit cards that show each soldier\

Bands with a single-target spell now cast it with every soldier: when the leader casts, each soldier strikes its own target with a share of the power, and comrades pick different enemies where they can

Bands across every contract: every 1-cost is now a regiment (summoners aside), most 2- and 3-costs too, and a few 4-costs are elite trios. Around three soldiers per unit at 1 to 3 cost, one at 4 and 5

Squads, first on The Ashward March: 29 units there are now bands of 3 to 5 soldiers, led by the named character (Hobb and his Pitchfork Levy, Kael and the Ash Grunts, Wat and his Yeomen, Captain Edda and her Burnt Levy veterans and more)
The battlefield is twice as big: 21 hexes long and 11 deep, with nine ranks a side
The Revenant General\
A new economy: prices are 25 times finer, so a 4-cost costs 100, a reroll 50 and each battle pays 75 (25 more for a win)
Battle report: after every fight, see damage dealt, damage taken and healing for each of your units (Report button, or R)
Proper desktop support: on computer screens the whole game scales up crisply to fill the window, with readable text at any size from laptops to 4K
Marching to an encounter refreshes the shop too, and it opens when you return to your board
The shop keeps its recruits after a fight and refreshes (and opens) when you march into the next battle
Every unit now has its own ability, built from its origin and class: 130 new spells, from Ironpact shield-shoves and Mirefolk ambushes to Inquisition stakes, Skald sagas and Verdant fairy rings
Every trait now has a signature move. Ravagers leap to the weakest enemy after a kill; Specters vanish and crit; Hexblades charge their next attacks after casting
Ironpact sign a contract before every battle (win fast, lose no one, score kills, keep your company standing) and get paid when they fulfil it
No more gold cap: save as much as you like (interest still tops out at 5)
The three- and four-star contracts (III to VI) now run four acts, and the later acts ramp up hard: tougher, better-equipped armies and stronger final bosses

Two new contracts. The Witch-Hunt (now Contract IV; the Cinder Throne becomes V): the Inquisition, militia and the faithful against witches, crows and burnt-out mages, ending at the Great Pyre with the Witch-Queen

Signature spell effects: pillars of light and lightning strikes, crashing waves, void vortexes, bursting roots, rot and spore clouds, ground-splitting quakes, shield domes, souls drained across the field, falling meteors, curse sigils, claw rakes and executioner\

Summons each have a role: drowned brutes (1/1/2) are huge tanks, shades (1/1/2) leap onto the weakest enemy, the Rat-King calls swarms of rats (2/3/4), pages cut from range (3/3/4), crows dive the back line (3/4/5), pufflings burst into healing spores
A shop unit that would star up shows the stars it would reach in its corner
Creatures attack properly: a wind-up, then a lunge, pounce or bite
About 40% more fights on the map, with fewer special stops; difficulty is stretched to match
Shields now fade: a shield lasts 4 seconds after it was last gained (8 for shields at the start of battle)
Each contract is now its own TFT-style set of eight origins and eight classes; most units have one origin and one class
A wider battlefield: 13 columns, five ranks per side and a no-man\
The game is now fully landscape: hold your phone sideways. If it is held upright, the whole game is drawn turned so it still plays sideways
Even fights: enemy boards now grow with the rounds to match yours, so battles are close and tense instead of lopsided
A bigger battlefield: taller phones spend their spare height on deeper rows and larger fighters
The Ashward March ramps up more gently
Everything moves by dragging: drag items onto units to equip them, and drag units to place, swap or sell them
The interface stays clear of the iPhone notch and camera cutout on every screen
Boot Camp tips now pause the game: the screen dims around what the tip points at, and you tap Got it to continue
Boot Camp: a two-act tutorial contract with a tip for every part of the game
The game always fetches the newest release, and offers a one-tap update if an old copy is showing
Sentinel reworked: Sentinels mark what they shoot, and the trait makes all your ranged units faster and longer-reaching
Trait names are back on shop cards
29 new units (110 in all): every contract can now reach the top tier of each of its origins and classes
Three new contracts from the design doc: Roads of the Drowned, The Festering Road and Siege of the Cinder Throne
Main menu with Continue, version history and sound settings
Covenant origin, one-screen map and flatter hexes
First web release: pixel-art company, items and the three-act campaign
